model_interpretation.claim: An 8x16 register-tiled AVX-512 FMA kernel should accelerate the large GEMM relative to the measured serial baseline. B-only 128x128 panels may improve reuse for larger matrices, but their per-call allocation and packing cost could offset that benefit; the same tile kernel uses direct B access below a generic two-panel threshold. A later matched-size direct-versus-packed run is needed to isolate the packing effect.

items.subject: Register-tiled SIMD GEMM with measured packing ablation
items.objective: Explore an explicit register-tiled FP32 FMA/SIMD microkernel with OpenMP ownership of disjoint output tiles. Measure direct-access and packed-panel variants using the same microkernel and comparable tiles where practical, so packing overhead and benefit are tested rather than assumed; consider packing B alone versus additional panels. Tune microkernel shape and panel layout, and include scratch allocation and packing in total runtime. Use AVX-512 or AVX2 only when compatible with the frozen GCC build and target, without changing compiler settings. Handle tails and small sizes generically, respect the threads budget (at most eight), fully overwrite output each invocation, and validate varying signed inputs against the fixed FP64 tolerance. Change only src/candidate.cpp; record failed attempts and report correctness and repeated native timings, prioritizing n=1024.
